name: Sequence Adaptive Multimodal SEGmentation (SAMSEG)
purpose: Robustly segment dozens of brain structures from head MRI scans without preprocessing, accepting multi-contrast data without prior assumptions on scanner or pulse sequences.
species_scope: human (implied by brain MRI and MS context)

inputs.statement: One or more co-registered MRI volumes in Nifti (.nii/.nii.gz) or FreeSurfer (.mgz) format.
inputs.quote: takes one or more co-registered MRI volumes as input

inputs.statement: All input volumes must be co-registered with each other and have the same image grid size and voxel dimensions.
inputs.quote: the only requirement is that all input volumes are co-registered with each other, and have the same image grid size and voxel dimensions

inputs.statement: For multi-contrast data, it is recommended to select the contrast with the highest spatial resolution and reformat all other contrasts to that grid.
inputs.quote: it is recommended to select the contrast with the highest spatial resolution (smallest voxel size) and reformat all other contrasts to that

inputs.statement: For longitudinal processing, all time points must be co-registered and reformatted to the same image grid, using an unbiased reference template.
inputs.quote: longitudinal SAMSEG expects all its input images to have been co-registered and reformatted to the same image grid beforehand

conditions.statement: Preprocessing with FreeSurfer is neither required nor recommended for basic SAMSEG.
conditions.quote: Preprocessing of the scan(s) with FreeSurfer is neither required nor recommended

conditions.statement: For multi-contrast input, all volumes must be co-registered and have the same image grid size and voxel dimensions.
conditions.quote: all input volumes are co-registered with each other, and have the same image grid size and voxel dimensions

conditions.statement: For longitudinal SAMSEG, the same combination of contrasts must be provided for each time point.
conditions.quote: SAMSEG expects that the same combination of contrasts is provided for each time point

conditions.statement: When using the lesion flag, the lesion-mask-pattern is optional but strongly recommended.

steps.statement: Run run_samseg with --input specifying one or more co-registered MRI volumes and --output specifying the output directory.
Optionally set --threads to the number of CPU cores for faster run time.
steps.quote: Set the number of threads to the number of CPU cores on your computer to get the fastest run time

steps.statement: Add --pallidum-separate if the input contrasts include those where the pallidum is clearly discernible, e.g., T2w or FLAIR.
steps.quote: if your combination of input volumes includes contrasts where the pallidum is clearly discernible (e.g., T2w or FLAIR) you should add this flag

steps.statement: For MS lesion segmentation, add --lesion and optionally --lesion-mask-pattern with one number per input contrast.
steps.quote: --lesion: is the flag to tell SAMSEG to segment white matter lesions

steps.statement: For longitudinal processing, first compute a robust average template using mri_robust_template, then run run_samseg_long with --timepoint for each time point.
steps.quote: mri_robust_template --mov tp0_t1.nii tp1_t1.nii tp2_t1.nii --template mean.mgz --satit --mapmov tp0_t1_reg.mgz tp1_t1_reg.mgz tp2_t1_reg.mgz

steps.statement: For multi-contrast longitudinal data, co-register each additional contrast to the corresponding reformatted T1w scan using mri_coreg and mri_vol2vol.
steps.quote: for each time additionally co-registering each FLAIR scan to the corresponding reformatted T1w scan

steps.statement: For longitudinal MS patients, add the same lesion flags as in cross-sectional processing.
steps.quote: Segmenting white matter lesions in MS with longitudinal SAMSEG is accomplished simply by adding the same flags as for the cross-sectional version

checks.statement: Verify that all input volumes are co-registered and have the same image grid size and voxel dimensions.
checks.quote: the only requirement is that all input volumes are co-registered with each other, and have the same image grid size and voxel dimensions

checks.statement: For longitudinal processing, ensure that the same combination of contrasts is provided for each time point.
checks.quote: SAMSEG expects that the same combination of contrasts is provided for each time point

checks.statement: When using the lesion flag, verify that the lesion-mask-pattern has one number for each input contrast.
checks.quote: The pattern is a sequence of numbers, one number for each input contrast

exceptions.statement: The pallidum is treated internally as a white matter structure by default because it typically cannot be discerned easily from white matter in T1w scans.
exceptions.quote: by default SAMSEG will treat the pallidum internally as a white matter structure, since it typically can't be discerned easily from white matter in T1w scans

exceptions.statement: The first time the MS lesion module is run, the user may be prompted to install Tensorflow.
exceptions.quote: The first time you run this module, you may be prompted to install Tensorflow

exceptions.statement: For longitudinal processing, simply reformatting all follow-up time points to the baseline scan would introduce a longitudinal processing bias.
exceptions.quote: simply reformatting all follow-up time points to the baseline scan would introduce a longitudinal processing bias

outputs.statement: seg.mgz: output segmentation volume where each voxel is assigned to one anatomical structure.
outputs.quote: seg.mgz: is the output segmentation volume, where each voxel has been assigned to one anatomical structure

outputs.statement: samseg.stats: contains the estimated volume in cubic mm for each segmented structure.
outputs.quote: samseg.stats: contains the estimated volume (in cubic mm) for each segmented structure

outputs.statement: mode0X_bias_corrected.mgz: the bias field corrected MRI volume corresponding to each input contrast.
outputs.quote: mode0X_bias_corrected.mgz (with X=1,2,...): the bias field corrected MRI volume corresponding to each input contrast

outputs.statement: mode0X_bias_field.mgz: the estimated bias field for each input contrast.
outputs.quote: mode0X_bias_field.mgz (with X=1,2,...): the estimated bias field for each input contrast

parameters.statement: --threads: number of threads to be used by SAMSEG; default uses one thread.
parameters.quote: <threads> (optional): is the number of threads to be used by SAMSEG (default uses one thread)

parameters.statement: --pallidum-separate: optional flag to treat the pallidum as a separate structure when contrasts make it discernible.
parameters.quote: --pallidum-separate (optional): by default SAMSEG will treat the pallidum internally as a white matter structure

parameters.statement: --lesion-mask-pattern: optional but strongly recommended; a sequence of numbers, one per input contrast, indicating intensity constraints relative to cortical gray matter.
parameters.quote: The pattern is a sequence of numbers, one number for each input contrast, with the following meaning: a value of "-1" or "1" indicates the voxels should be darker or brighter than cortical gray matter

parameters.statement: --threshold: optional threshold applied to the probability of a voxel being lesion; default is 0.3 in the current implementation.
parameters.quote: The default value (0.3 in the current implementation) will typically give reasonable results

claim.statement: Optionally set --threshold to adjust the balance between false positive and false negative lesion detections.
claim.quote: you can tweak this value (between 0.0 and 1.0) to obtain a more fine-grained balance between false positive and false negative lesion detections

claim.statement: The blog example is a single-subject test and does not constitute validation or general applicability.
claim.quote: 注意这只是一个被试数据的结果
